svg.title: AscendFlow: explicit kernels, automatic synchronization
svg.desc: The author chooses stage offsets and physical buffers. For aligned D128 attention, QK and softmax have offset 0; PV and store have offset 1. Score, P and PV each have two independent GM slots indexed by tile modulo two. The compiler derives producer readiness and last-reader release. Each actor expands tile equals its own local step minus stage, yielding fill, steady issue and drain. Cube and Vector local counters are independent and the table is not a wall-clock trace.
svg.text: Explicit computation and scheduling. Synchronization from real memory use.
1 Choose stage offsets and physical buffers
Stage = offset in an actor’s own issue loop
Per actor: visit stage 0, then stage 1.
Three independent rings · K/V resident in L0
2 Derive ready and release from the real accesses
Score[s]: retire both AIV GM reads
PV[s]: retire both AIV GM reads
ready: finish writing t → allow its readers
release: last reader of t retires → allow writer of t+2
3 Expand tile = local_step − stage; activate only 0 ≤ tile < 4
Cube uses j_C; Vector uses j_V. Each counter advances independently, subject to ready / release.
Steady state: Cube QK(j_C) → PV(j_C−1) | Vector softmax(j_V) → store(j_V−1)
Within each actor, → means issue order. Across actors, matching columns do not mean simultaneous execution.
Stage offsets select logical generations. Buffer slots select physical storage. Waits preserve both contracts.
Aligned non-causal attention · D128 / Q tile64 / KV128 · conceptual issue expansion, not a latency trace
